solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Top set of administrators right for the navy?

parts.note: a star is a top performer, the best of the bunch
a board is the body of directors running an organisation

explanation.surface: A question about whether an elite committee would suit the Royal Navy.
explanation.definitionFit: Sailors call the right-hand side of a vessel, looking forward, by this nautical term.

clue.text: Quotes, to those who'd hear, tourist attractions?

indicators.note: to those who'd hear says the word is taken by its sound

parts.note: to cite is to quote, so cites means quotes

explanation.surface: A guide's remark that, if you listen, quotations are the real attractions.
explanation.definitionFit: Places worth seeing on a trip are what visitors go to see in a town.

clue.text: Month on front of stage

parts.note: Apr is the short form of April

explanation.surface: A month spent at the front of a theatre.
explanation.definitionFit: In a theatre the part of the stage in front of the curtain is called by this term.

clue.text: Deposit in different pubs — spent on these?

indicators.note: in puts the mud word inside the rearranged pubs
different says the letters of pubs are rearranged

parts.note: ooze is soft mud deposited on a river or sea bed

explanation.surface: Money paid into several pubs, all used up on drinking sessions.
explanation.walkthrough: 'different' rearranges the pubs into BUPS. Read as a whole, the clue also hints at where pub money goes.
explanation.definitionFit: Heavy drinking sessions are where money left in a pub goes, hence the playful question.

clue.text: Get aid for free, anyhow, and stop arguing

indicators.note: anyhow means in a random way, so the letters of the first four words are mixed up

explanation.surface: Advice to obtain free help somehow and end a quarrel.
explanation.definitionFit: Accepting that two sides hold different views is an idiom for ending a dispute.

clue.text: Right to stop moisture getting extracted

indicators.note: to stop means to plug or block, so the right letter goes into the moisture

parts.note: dew is moisture that condenses overnight

explanation.surface: An instruction to block damp being drawn out.
explanation.definitionFit: Drew in the sense of pulled out, as a tooth or a sword is drawn, is past tense of draw.

clue.text: Regret common currency being cut back

indicators.note: back says the shortened word is then read in the opposite direction
being cut tells us to drop the final letter of the currency word

parts.note: the euro is the currency shared by many European countries

explanation.surface: Someone laments that the shared European money has been devalued.
explanation.walkthrough: 'being cut' trims EURO to EUR, and 'back' turns that round.
explanation.definitionFit: To regret something is to be sorry about it, a sense this short verb carries.

clue.text: Beam outside a French church is rather dirty

indicators.note: outside says the beam word goes round the other pieces

parts.note: a ray is a beam of light
un is French for a

explanation.surface: A sunbeam falls on a grimy French church.
explanation.definitionFit: Dirty in the sense of smutty or sexually suggestive is what this adjective means.

clue.text: European representative with passion for his domain?

parts.note: an MP, Member of Parliament, is an elected representative
ire is anger, a passion

explanation.surface: A European politician with fierce feelings about his territory.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition leans on the surface: 'his' is the emperor implied by the picture.
explanation.definitionFit: A domain ruled over by an emperor is the realm of that sovereign; the question mark flags the indirect sense.

clue.text: Actress none boast about

indicators.note: about asks for the pair of pieces to be turned round end to end

parts.note: O, the figure nought, stands for none
to brag is to boast

explanation.surface: An actress who never shows off.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' turns O + BRAG round as a whole.
explanation.definitionFit: Greta Garbo was the Swedish-born Hollywood film star famed for wanting to be alone.

clue.text: Engineers joke about private in the end getting kit out again

parts.note: RE is the Royal Engineers, a corps of the British Army

indicators.note: in the end picks only the final letter of the word private

parts.note: a quip is a witty remark

explanation.surface: Army engineers banter with a private while being issued fresh gear.
explanation.definitionFit: To kit out is to equip, so doing it once more is a fresh supplying of gear.

clue.text: Tree: kind that's damaged and messed about

indicators.note: damaged suggests the letters of the first two words are knocked out of shape

explanation.surface: A gardener's note about a type of tree that has been harmed and interfered with.
explanation.definitionFit: To tinker is to fiddle with something in an unskilled way, i.e. to mess about with it.

clue.text: Mark short item of neckwear

indicators.note: short asks for the last letter of the neckwear word to be dropped

parts.note: a scarf is worn round the neck

explanation.surface: A stain on a little bit of clothing worn at the neck.
explanation.definitionFit: A lasting mark left on skin after a wound heals is this blemish.

clue.text: Parachutist getting kids very jazzed up

indicators.note: jazzed up means livened and altered, so the letters of the two words are mixed

explanation.surface: A parachutist gets the youngsters thoroughly excited.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who jumps from aircraft and freefalls before opening a chute is a parachutist.

clue.text: Contestants at Aintree, say, start manoeuvres

parts.note: to jump is to start in surprise
to jockey is to manoeuvre for position, so jockeys means manoeuvres

explanation.surface: Racing participants begin their tactical moves.
explanation.walkthrough: Aintree, near Liverpool, is the racecourse that stages the Grand National steeplechase.
explanation.definitionFit: Riders in steeplechases over fences, like the Grand National, are known by this term; 'say' marks Aintree as an example.

clue.text: Intimidate frontrunner, vexed to an extent

indicators.note: to an extent says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: Rattle the race leader, who is already somewhat annoyed.
explanation.definitionFit: To intimidate someone is to make them lose their nerve, a near synonym.

clue.text: Question cook cutting ends off tart

indicators.note: cutting ends off says each of the two words loses its last letter

parts.note: to quiz someone is to question them
a chef is a cook

explanation.surface: Interrogate a cook for trimming the pastry edges of a tart.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cutting ends off' trims QUIZ to QUI and CHEF to CHE.
explanation.definitionFit: A savoury open pastry case with an egg filling is a kind of tart.

clue.text: Time former partner and boy sent message

parts.note: an ex is a former partner
Ted is a boy's name

explanation.surface: Someone's old flame and a lad got in touch by phone.
explanation.definitionFit: To send a written message from a mobile phone is the verb here, in the past tense.

clue.text: Brings in, for audience, pots of tea?

indicators.note: for audience says the word is to be heard rather than read

parts.note: a person who earns money brings it in

explanation.surface: A tea room's takings come from serving tea.
explanation.walkthrough: The match works in a British accent with no sounded R.
explanation.definitionFit: Large metal vessels with taps are used to keep tea hot for crowds; the question mark flags the loose sense.

clue.text: Spooner's fastened tissue in part of throat

indicators.note: Spooner's tells us to swap the opening sounds of the two words, after the Reverend Spooner

parts.note: pinned means fastened with a pin
a wipe is a disposable cleaning tissue

explanation.surface: A tissue pinned in place somewhere in the neck.
explanation.walkthrough: Swapping P and W in PINNED WIPE gives WINNED PIPE, which is said like the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: The trachea, the tube carrying air to the lungs, is commonly given this name.

clue.text: At home, ready for mini-picture

parts.note: to be in is to be at home
set means ready, as in ready, steady, go

explanation.surface: At home and prepared for a small photograph.
explanation.definitionFit: A small picture set within a larger one, such as a map, is called this.

clue.text: Court orders, it's said, somewhere posh to stay

indicators.note: it's said tells us the word is taken by its sound

parts.note: writs are written court orders

explanation.surface: A judge's orders, so they say, send someone to a smart hotel.
explanation.definitionFit: The Ritz in London is a famously luxurious hotel, a byword for upmarket lodging.

clue.text: City ace, maybe, one starts to find fifth-rate

parts.note: an ace is an example of a playing card
I is the Roman numeral for one

indicators.note: starts to signals taking the first letters of the following two words

explanation.surface: A remark that a top city player finds the place inferior.
explanation.definitionFit: The Welsh capital is a city in south Wales.

clue.text: Come round squat after six

indicators.note: after places the crouching word behind the number

parts.note: VI is six in Roman numerals
to squat is to sit low

explanation.surface: An invitation to drop by and sit down once it has turned six o'clock.
explanation.definitionFit: To come round to someone's house is to call on them.

clue.text: River that often marks spot, it's said

indicators.note: it's said tells us to go by how the letter is pronounced

parts.note: X marks the spot, as on a treasure map

explanation.surface: A river that is a common landmark on maps.
explanation.walkthrough: The Exe flows through Devon in south-west England to Exeter.
explanation.definitionFit: The Exe is a river of south-west England, so it is an example of a waterway.

clue.text: Trader Zoe arranged to be tax exempt

indicators.note: arranged signals that the letters of the trader's name and job are put in a new order

explanation.surface: A merchant called Zoe has set things up so she pays no tax.
explanation.walkthrough: In UK VAT, goods charged at a 0% rate are described this way.
explanation.definitionFit: Goods taxed at a zero rate pay no VAT, so they are effectively untaxed.
